title: Escher Droste spiral
blurb: A live editable HTML card wrapped across ten or more scale octaves by a conformal complex-logarithm Escher Droste shader and a ping-pong mirror tunnel on one WebGL 2 canvas. Switch between bilinear, trilinear mipmaps and anisotropic filtering to compare legibility after texElementSubImage2D().
question: Can an analytic complex-logarithm Escher Droste spiral and an infinite ping-pong mirror tunnel wrap a live editable HTML card across 10+ octaves of scale, and do gl.generateMipmap() and anisotropic filtering work cleanly on a texElementSubImage2D() texture without shimmer or artefacts?
result: Not verified in a live browser yet. One ElementGL WebGL 2 context uploads the framed HTML card with texElementSubImage2D(), calls gl.generateMipmap(gl.TEXTURE_2D) and EXT_texture_filter_anisotropic, renders both the conformal Droste spiral (using analytic Jacobian textureGrad() sampling) and a two-FBO ping-pong mirror tunnel, and keeps controls interactive via updateElementGeometry().
